# s247 — A relay request must reach ai relay and confirm the setup with the owner

When an owner asks for a slice relay, an agent loads the slicer skill and should arrive at `slicer ai relay`. Before it creates the worktree, the relay should have it confirm the setup with the owner. Today neither happens. The skill never names the relay, and the relay text names no setup step, so the agent improvises the roles and the end point or follows outside guidance.

**Findings:** owner, session 2026-10-11 (s245 relay): skill never names ai relay; relay text has no setup step, so roles, models and end point were improvised from outside guidance · **Size:** S · **Trees:** src/slicer, tests, docs

**2026-10-11** — 2026-10-11 owner: the architect runs only on size-L slices (agents playbook 0413109). slicer stays policy-neutral: Setup and Order make the architect optional and owner-chosen; the size rule lives in the agents binding (layering decision: slicer ai relay = contract, agents playbook = binding).

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** reading any vendor or agents-repo config (relay.conf, playbooks); asking the setup questions in code (it stays guidance text); changing the gate, the roles or the close; the s245 `verify --landed` command.

## Why

Session 2026-10-11, s245: the owner said "start s245 in a slicer relay. ask me about setup to confirm (agent roles)". The agent loaded the skill. The skill says to run `slicer ai instructions --rest` only "for planning, filing, claims, and review", so the agent never reached the pointer that s244 added. It also never ran `slicer ai relay`. Instead it ran the relay from the agents-repo playbook and `relay.conf`, outside the workspace. The setup questions it asked came from the owner's prompt, not from slicer:

- which roles run (no architect on a size-S slice)
- which model each role uses
- where the run stops: after handoff, a commit on the branch, or landing

`RELAY` (`src/slicer/ai.py:144`) says "The owner chooses the models" but has no step that asks the owner. Its Order section starts at "Create a worktree". s244 kept the skill text unchanged on purpose, so installed copies would stay current. That left the skill as the one entry point without the pointer.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py`:
  - `skill_text()` (line 217): one line that sends a relay request to `slicer ai relay`.
  - `RELAY`: a "Setup" section placed before "Order". Before the worktree exists, the orchestrator reads the slice's size and confirms three things with the owner:
    - which roles run. The architect is optional: the owner decides, and slicer states no size policy. Size rules belong to the binding that runs the relay, for example the agents-repo playbook.
    - the vendor, model and effort per role
    - where the run ends: after the finish step, after a commit on the slice branch, or landed. Land only when the owner asks.

    The section names no vendor, model or file outside slicer.
  - `RELAY` Order: name the architect as optional ("the architect, when the owner chose one"), so a run without one still follows the Order.
- `.claude/skills/slicer/SKILL.md` and any other committed skill copies, regenerated with `slicer ai skill`.
- `docs/agents.md` (the relay and skill rows), if they quote either text. `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_ai.py`.
